task.title: 9-doc audit: support docs/ locations, recognise MADR decision records, recommend MADR as default

acceptance_criteria: SCOPE. The audit currently resolves the nine documents by root-relative filename and enforces drift for boundary types in SPEC.md. To let a repository put docs in docs/ it needs: (1) configurable document locations
resolved per repo rather than hardcoded
ideally from the unified .gaugeblock/config.toml [docs] section that BW-32 repaired; (2) a MADR recogniser for docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md - validating front matter (status
unique four-digit numbering and an index that lists every record
since an unlisted ADR is a decision nobody will find; (3) 'recommend MADR as default' = the audit suggests it when a repo has architectural decisions living in prose inside ARCHITECTURE.md
and scaffold creates docs/decisions/0001-*.md on init.\n\nSEQUENCING: this must land BEFORE GB-275 moves any files. The audit is what gates document location today
so moving ARCHITECTURE.md and friends into docs/ first would turn twelve clean audits into twelve violations

and the temptation would be to silence the gate rather than teach it. Same ordering rule that made GB-267 precede GB-263 and GB-261 Phase 5 follow GB-268: change the instrument before the thing it measures.

RE-SCOPED 2026-11-06, much smaller than filed. The audit is already config-driven: DocType::default_filename supplies defaults and .gaugeblock/docs.toml overrides a path per document type, which the audit honours. So configurable locations are DONE, and no chalkline change is needed for the docs move - proven on rabbet, which moved six documents and audited 9/0/0 with only a docs.toml and link repairs.

That leaves exactly one piece of real code in this ticket: MADR recognition for docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md - front matter (status, date, decision-makers), required sections, unique four-digit numbering, and an index that lists every record. Plus scaffolding docs/decisions/ on init so a new repository starts with the convention rather than discovering it later.

'Recommend MADR as default' is a doc-and-audit change, not a code change: the audit should suggest it when architectural decisions live in prose inside ARCHITECTURE.md, which it can already read.

SEQUENCING unchanged and now cheap: the docs move (GB-275) does NOT need to wait for the MADR recogniser, because the move needs no chalkline change at all.

RECOGNISER DONE 2026-11-06 (chalkline commit). chalkline_core::docs::decisions::audit_decision_records validates docs/decisions/: NNNN-slug.md naming, four-digit unique numbering, --- front matter with status and date, 'Context and Problem Statement' and 'Decision Outcome' sections, and an index (README.md or INDEX.md) that lists every record. Wired into 'chalkline docs check' as its own reported section, and findings fail the audit. Verified: rabbet audits 9/0/0 with no decision section because it has no docs/decisions, which is correct - absence is not a violation. 5 tests, clippy clean, workspace tests green.

Kept out of DocType::ALL deliberately: the nine documents are a fixed one-per-type contract, decision records are an unbounded set with different rules, and a tenth variant would distort every count derived from that list.

REMAINING: (1) scaffold docs/decisions/README.md on init so a new repository starts with the convention; (2) the suite root needs its own docs/decisions for cross-repo contract decisions (the JSON envelope decision GB-274, the one-backlog decision D7, and the ledger-location rule are all ready to be written as the first three ADRs); (3) decide whether the 'promote a storypole decision into an ADR' step is worth building or whether decisions stay in the ledger and ADRs are written deliberately.

SCAFFOLD DONE 2026-11-06: `chalkline docs scaffold` creates docs/decisions/README.md with the ordering rule and the MADR shape stated inside the file itself, on the reasoning that the next author reads that index rather than a conventions document. Verified on a fresh temporary repository (scaffold exit 0, file created). Scaffolded separately from the nine documents because they are one-per-type and decision records are an unbounded set.

EPIC GB-275/GB-276 STATUS: docs move complete across eleven repositories (108/108 clean); MADR recogniser enforced including chronological ordering; first five ADRs backfilled in decision-date order; scaffolding in place. REMAINING: none required - what is left is optional (member-repo decision directories where a repository has its own cross-cutting decisions, and the question of whether storypole decisions should auto-promote into ADRs, which I would leave as a deliberate manual act so an ADR is always someone's considered statement rather than a mechanical echo).
